finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role: requireRole returns a boolean that is discarded, so any caller (including one with an empty role set) can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: User u argument and attacker-chosen tenant parameter on POST /tenants/{t}/wipe (any caller that reaches wipe)

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point
requireRole(u, "OWNER") evaluates u.roles().contains("OWNER") but the boolean result is discarded
requireRole is a non-throwing predicate (Javadoc at line 13 says so)

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns boolean and is ignored by caller; checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws on failure but is not used in wipe; no other check in file. Repro: new Admin().wipe(new User("x", Set.of()), "victim") calls repo.wipe("victim").

verdict.guard_found: None effective. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean, and its result is discarded by the bare call at src/Admin.java:26. checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) would throw, but wipe does not call it (export at line 32 does). No other file in the directory defines a route, filter, or check that gates wipe(); the only "tenants" reference is the comment at line 24.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 calls the non-throwing boolean requireRole and discards its result, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any User, including one with an empty role set, and nothing else in the directory enforces the OWNER check.

finding.claim: Role checks are not scoped to the target tenant: a user holding OWNER in any tenant can export (and, via F1's pattern, wipe) any other tenant's data.
finding.source: User u holding OWNER in some tenant, plus attacker-chosen tenant parameter
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33 (cross-tenant data export); repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 also affected

trace.note: export(User u, String tenant) entry point
checkRole(u, "OWNER") passes if global roles set contains OWNER; tenant is not compared to user's tenant membership
repo.export(tenant) runs for any tenant name
User record has only name and roles; no tenant field, so roles cannot be tenant-scoped in this file

finding.guards_checked: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) verifies a global role only; no tenant-membership or ownership lookup in this file. Exploitability depends on upstream caller restricting tenant to the user's own tenants, which is not in this directory (confidence: plausible).

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) is a real gate: it throws SecurityException when the user's global roles lack "OWNER". No tenant-membership or ownership check exists in src/Admin.java, and the only other file in the directory is Admin.java itself, so no upstream caller is visible.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: export() at src/Admin.java:31-33 checks only a global OWNER role at line 32 and then calls repo.export(tenant) with no comparison against the user's tenants, and User (line 4) has no tenant field. Whether an OWNER in one tenant can reach another tenant's export depends on how roles are scoped and how the HTTP layer restricts the {t} parameter, and neither is in this directory, so the finding can be neither confirmed nor refuted here. Separately, wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 discards requireRole's boolean result, so wipe has no authorization at all; that is a stronger issue than F2, but it belongs to F1.
